newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - FKI bows out of Newman Tonks battle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - FKI bows out of Newman Tonks battle.

text.p: British engineering firm FKI Plc on Wednesday threw in the towel in its fight for Newman Tonks Group Plc, clearing the way for U.S. rival Ingersoll-Rand Co to win control of the company.

FKI said it was allowing its hostile 195.7 million pound ($316.9 million) bid for the British building products group to lapse, just two days after Ingersoll-Rand unveiled a 230 million pound cash offer, which was recommended by Newman's board.
Ingersoll is a multinational manufacturer of industrial machinery.
FKI said Newman had given it confidential information after Ingersoll-Rand's bid, but added that the information contained nothing to justify raising its cash-and-share offer.

"Having carefully studied the confidential information supplied to us, it is clear that a higher offer would not create sufficient value for our shareholders, and we have therefore decided to lapse our offer," FKI chairman Jeff Whalley said in a statement.
"FKI will continue to pursue its strategy of delivering value to its shareholders by strengthening core businesses and making acquisitions at a sensible price that fit," he added.
FKI also said it would not proceed with its planned 2-for-13 rights issue, which was intended to raise up to 152.4 million pounds to help finance the acquisition.
Newman Tonks' shares slipped 2.0 pence to close at 178.5 while FKI firmed 2.5 pence to 197.5.
In the U.S., Ingersoll-Rand's shares gained $1 to $44-1/4.
FKI's withdrawal paved the way for the U.S. industrial machinery maker to succeed in its bid, which offered 175 pence for every Newman Tonks share.
On Tuesday, Ingersoll-Rand said its NT Acquisition Ltd unit had bought 4.9 million shares in Newman, representing 3.82 percent of the company's ordinary shares.
When it unveiled its surprise offer, Ingersoll-Rand said Newman would help shape its European strategy.
"It will serve us better in the fast-growing Asian markets as well," Ingersoll-Rand vice president Brian Jellison told Reuters on Monday.
Newman previously forecast profits before tax, exceptional items and bid costs of not less than 18 million pounds for the year to December 31, 1996.
Newman's 1995 pretax profit stood at 27.2 million pounds.
FKI said Newman shareholders who had accepted its offer would be released from such acceptances.
Earlier this week, FKI said it had received acceptances for about 20.6 percent of Newman's ordinary shares and also agreed to buy stock representing another 0.4 percent. ($1=.6175 Pound)
